payload.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): Unblocked: PR #2871 merged 2026-09-18 (4f1994eb5) and the app:///_next route recovery is on main (error-tracking.ts). 'Waits on #2871' and 'do not set those Railway variables until #2871 lands' are stale; the 24-hour Sentry re-read is now due (provider read). The source-map and variables paragraph now lives in #BPPRG2. PRIOR DETAIL: NEXT ACTION, once PR #2853 has deployed and roughly 24h of events have accumulated: re-read Sentry project clinibase-xz/javascript-nextjs and name the faulting code. Expect the 20 open groups sharing the title Unhandled server request error to collapse to one or two with counts that finally mean something. Use the restored capture mechanism (handled vs onunhandledrejection) to tell a crash from a reported error, and the route recovered into the fingerprint to locate it. WHY IT WAS NOT DIAGNOSABLE BEFORE, measured 2026-09-17: 853 of 857 error events in the preceding 30 days carried no route_path tag, so they took the undefined fingerprint branch in privacySafeErrorEvent and Sentry regrouped them on minified frames that change every build; and the scrubber dropped the exception mechanism, so all 857 events reported error.handled 1 regardless of origin. PR #2853 fixed both. NOT BLOCKING but makes frames readable: source-map upload stays inert until an operator sets SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG (clinibase-xz) and SENTRY_PROJECT (javascript-nextjs) on the Railway Database service. PR #2853 declared the matching Dockerfile build ARGs, without which those variables would have been a silent no-op. ALREADY EXCLUDED, do not re-investigate: JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-2D (4 events, /differentials/diagnoses/[slug], route_type render) is a reader disconnecting during a streaming page render, stack entirely Next internals, not worth acting on. DO NOT RE-FOLLOW the original supplied analysis, which blamed AbortErrors escaping four API routes: that was checked against the code and is wrong, because jsonError returns a Response so onRequestError never fires. One incidental observation worth a glance: every sampled event reported user.geo SG, Singapore. CORRECTED 2026-09-18: the figures above were first recorded as 849 of 853, which was wrong -- 853 was the untagged count, not the population. Re-read from Sentry as two separate aggregates rather than one derived figure: event.type:error returns 857 and event.type:error !has:route_path returns 853. STATUS CHANGE, also 2026-09-18: PR #2853 was squash-merged at the commit before its final push, so the fixes this row depends on are NOT all on main. Three adversarial reviews found four defects in it, and PR #2871 restores them. Two matter to this row. First, main recovers the route by matching only the /app/.next spelling, so setting the three Sentry build variables would make the SDK DistDirRewriteFrames integration rewrite every frame to app:///_next and collapse the whole application into one unrouted bucket -- worse than the splintering being fixed. DO NOT set those Railway variables until #2871 lands. Second, route-group directories such as (search-app) are kept in the recovered pattern where captureRequestError own tag omits them, so a page fault still splits into two groups. The NEXT ACTION above therefore waits on #2871 deploying, not #2853.
